mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 5% over two consecutive months signals a tightening monetary regime, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods when FEDFUNDS > 5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a rise in the unemployment rate above 5% signals weakening aggregate demand, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during episodes where GDPC1 YoY < -2% and UNRATE > 5%.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase of more than 0.4 percentage points in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is followed by negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days due to heightened recession risk and corporate earnings downgrades.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) following a monthly UNRATE increase > 0.4pp.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% for three consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during three-month INDPRO declines > 1%.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise of at least 0.5% in the Housing Starts Index (HOUST) and a year-over-year increase of at least 3% in Personal Income Less Transfer (proxied by RSAFS) signals a robust housing demand recovery, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) during episodes of concurrent HOUST > +0.5% and RSAFS YoY > 3%.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is held constant for three consecutive months at or below 3%, liquidity conditions remain accommodative, supporting equity valuations and resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS unchanged for 3 consecutive months AND FEDFUNDS <= 3%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) when FEDFUNDS is unchanged at or below 3% for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly payroll employment increase (PAYEMS) below 50,000 persons for two consecutive months signals weak labor market momentum, which is associated with negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to earnings downgrades.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during two-month periods of PAYEMS < 50,000.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly decline of at least 0.3% in both the Industrial Production Index (INDPRO) and Real Personal Consumption Expenditures (GDPC1) signals broad-based demand contraction, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) when both INDPRO and GDPC1 decline by at least 0.3% month-over-month.
